questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Slope of the Tangent at a Point of a Function Involving Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
questions.problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{3}$ if $f(x)=11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+{x}^{-1}) \\  & =11(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\sqrt{3}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\sqrt{3}) & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =-11\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cotangent Function
questions.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\operatorname{cot}⁡(x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡(x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)(-{csc}^{2}⁡(x)) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cot}⁡(x)}{x}-\operatorname{ln}⁡(x){csc}^{2}⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cotangent Function
questions.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{cot}⁡(x)) \\  & =1\operatorname{cot}⁡(x)+x(-{csc}^{2}⁡(x)) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(x)-x{csc}^{2}⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Secant Function
questions.worked_solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\,(2\operatorname{sec}⁡(x)-{4}^{x}) \\  & =2\operatorname{sec}⁡(x)\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)-{4}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡4\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Slope of the Tangent at a Point of a Function Involving Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}+3\operatorname{sec}⁡x) \\  & ={e}^{x}+3\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute $x=\pi $ and evaluate the slope $m:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m={h}^{′}(\pi ) & ={e}^{\pi }+3\operatorname{sec}⁡(\pi )\operatorname{tan}⁡(\pi ) \\  & ={e}^{\pi }+3\cdot (-1)\cdot 0 \\  & ={e}^{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$
